input: With the standby pump running and proved to be carrying the duty, the duty pump is to be taken out of service and isolated so that the seal can be replaced. The duty pump is stopped at its local switch, and the switch is locked in the off position so that the pump cannot be restarted while the work is in progress. The suction and discharge valves on the duty pump are then closed and fitted with their valve locks, and each valve is recorded on the isolation certificate as it is closed, in the order in which it is dealt with. A try-start of the duty pump is made once the lockout is complete, in order to prove that the isolation is effective. The casing of the pump is drained by opening the drain at the casing and allowing the contents to run to the closed drain system, and the vent at the high point of the casing is opened and is left open for so long as the seal is out of the pump. It must be clearly understood that the casing and the seal housing are capable of retaining stored pressure even after the pump has been stopped and the valves have been closed, and the casing is therefore to be proved depressured at the vent before any attempt is made to slacken a seal bolt. The work on the seal itself is carried out under a PTW, and the whole of the seal replacement takes about 69 min with the unit isolated. Throughout this period the standby pump is kept running, with its suction and discharge valves proved open, and the drain and the vent on the isolated pump are left open. The fitter works only within the boundary that the isolation establishes, namely the seal housing together with the casing drain and vent connections, and pipework lying outside the closed valves forms no part of the isolation and is not to be opened.
target: Transfer the duty to the standby pump and prove the standby pump is carrying it before the duty pump is touched. Stop the duty pump at its local switch and lock the switch in the off position. Close the suction and discharge valves on the duty pump and fit the valve locks. Record each valve on the isolation certificate as it is closed, in the order the valves are closed. Try the start switch once after lockout to prove the isolation holds. Open the drain at the pump casing and drain the casing to the closed drain system. Open the vent at the high point of the casing and leave the vent open while the seal is out. Inform the control room that the duty pump is out of service and that the standby pump is carrying the duty, and keep the locked switch key with the isolation certificate until the work is finished and the isolation is formally handed back. The casing and the seal housing can hold stored pressure after the pump is stopped and the valves are closed: prove the casing depressured at the vent before any seal bolt is slackened. Work on the seal proceeds under a PTW. The seal replacement takes about 69 min with the unit isolated. Leave the drain and the vent open for the whole of the work. Keep the standby pump running throughout, with its suction and discharge valves proved open. Prove the casing empty by the flow at the drain before the vent is relied on as the proof of depressuring. Work only inside the boundary the isolation sets: the seal housing and the casing drain and vent connections. Pipework outside the closed valves is not part of the isolation and is not opened. The isolation stays in force until the seal work is complete, the housing is closed up, and the casing has been proved ready to be filled again.
